To improve my chances, I need to consider a strategic ranking. Since y is so popular, and I am only rank 1 at w, I should consider ranking y first. This might give me a better chance of getting matched, as many applicants will be competing for y. If I get rejected from y, my next best option is w, where I have the highest priority (rank 1). Then z, and finally x.

This strategy acknowledges the popularity of y and attempts to capitalize on my strong position at w if y doesn't work out. It's a gamble, but potentially a better one than leading with w and likely being rejected by both w and y.
